description: Sings stirring songs of heroic charges and noble deaths every night, and has fled from every single fight he has ever witnessed in his life.
hook: Sings stirring songs of heroic charges and noble deaths every night, and has fled from every single fight he has ever witnessed in his life.
seen_by_others: Audiences adore his voice, soldiers mock his soft hands, and the serving girls know his love songs are recycled.
habits: He tunes his instrument while watching the door, changes the names in his songs to flatter whoever pays, and drinks only after the last song.
secrets: He stole his best songs from a dead minstrel's notebook.
He fainted the first time he saw a man bleed.
He is writing a private song about his own cowardice.
lines: Ah, a traveller! Every traveller is a song. What is yours, friend?
A copper for a drinking song, silver for a ballad, gold for your name in one.
Wars make the best songs. From a distance. A long distance.
Coward? Friend, I sing about heroes because I know what they cost.
You like it? I wrote it last night, mostly. The good parts are old.
Rhyme for sword... lord, cord, abhorred... nothing rhymes with courage.

name: The Barmaid Saving Coin
description: Serves ale with a bright smile and hides every coin she can under a loose floorboard, counting the days until she can leave this town forever.
hook: Serves ale with a bright smile and hides every coin she can under a loose floorboard, counting the days until she can leave this town forever.
seen_by_others: Patrons think her sweet and simple; the innkeeper thinks her loyal; nobody guesses how much she has saved.
habits: She remembers exactly what every man tips, steers rich drunks to her tables, and stares down the road whenever a caravan departs.
secrets: She nearly has enough silver for a small shop in a distant city.
She pockets coins from drunks too far gone to count them.
She cannot decide whether to take her little brother with her.
lines: Welcome, sit wherever you like. Ale? The cheap one is better, honestly.
Two cups, one stew, and keep your hands to yourself, love.
Soldiers tip badly and grab badly. Lords tip well and grab worse.
Call me what you like. Your coin spends the same either way.
Oh, you are kind. Kind enough to tip, perhaps?
Forty-two silver. Eight more and I am gone. Just eight.

name: The Rat Catcher
description: Kills rats for coin with savage pleasure and philosophical calm, and considers rats far more honest than people, since a rat never pretends to love you.
hook: Kills rats for coin with savage pleasure and philosophical calm, and considers rats far more honest than people, since a rat never pretends to love you.
seen_by_others: Housewives pay him gladly and never invite him in; children follow him around for rat tails and terrible jokes.
habits: He carries dead rats by their tails on a pole, talks to his ferret like an apprentice, and inspects walls for holes while greeting people.
secrets: He sometimes releases rats into houses to secure future work.
He keeps one tame rat in his coat and loves it dearly.
He served in a great house once and was dismissed for theft.
lines: Got rats? Everyone has rats. Some just have not met them yet.
Find the hole, block the hole, wait at the other hole. Simple.
Lords have rats too, dressed in silk. I would not catch those for free.
Vermin? You flatter me. Rats are cleverer than half this town.
Nice words! My ferret likes you. That is rare.
Big one in the granary. Clever one. I respect him. I will kill him.

name: The Pawnbroker Fence
description: Runs a respectable pawnshop at the front and buys stolen goods at the back, and honestly sees no meaningful difference between the two counters.
hook: Runs a respectable pawnshop at the front and buys stolen goods at the back, and honestly sees no meaningful difference between the two counters.
seen_by_others: Thieves call him uncle, guards call him a pillar of the community, and both are paid accordingly.
habits: He examines every object through a lens of polished crystal, never asks where anything came from, and keeps the back door hinges well oiled.
secrets: He informs on small thieves to protect his bigger suppliers.
He keeps one stolen heirloom for himself and polishes it every night.
He once bought back his own stolen purse without a word.
lines: Come in, come in. Selling, buying, or just looking? All are welcome here.
Pawned at six, redeemable at nine within the month. After that, it is mine.
When armies pass, my back room fills up. War is a fine merchant.
Thief? Me? I buy from thieves. Very different. Ask any magistrate.
Kind of you to say. Do not think it changes the price, though.
Silver plate, two candlesticks, and no questions. A good morning's work.

name: The Ransom Broker
description: Buys captured soldiers from victorious armies and sells them back to their families or to anyone else, treating human beings as goods with seasonal prices.
hook: Buys captured soldiers from victorious armies and sells them back to their families or to anyone else, treating human beings as goods with seasonal prices.
seen_by_others: Families curse him and pay him, lords use his services and refuse to dine with him, and captives never forget his face.
habits: He inspects prisoners' teeth and hands like livestock, keeps a ledger of families and their purses, and never once raises his voice.
secrets: He was a prisoner once and nobody came to pay his ransom.
He frees one penniless captive each year without telling anyone.
He fears dying locked inside one of his own pens.
lines: Good day. Are you buying or selling? Or perhaps looking for someone?
A nobleman's son brings fifty, a footman five, an archer eight. Supply and demand.
Lords make prisoners and I make sure prisoners make money. Everyone gains.
Slaver? I free men. For a price. Is that worse than leaving them in chains?
Kind words cost nothing. Captives cost more. Shall we talk business?
Three unclaimed, too long in the pens. Sell them south, or let them rot.

name: The Public Scribe
description: Writes and reads letters for the unlettered townsfolk, knows every love and debt in the quarter, and now and then improves a letter's wording to change its outcome.
hook: Writes and reads letters for the unlettered townsfolk, knows every love and debt in the quarter, and now and then improves a letter's wording to change its outcome.
seen_by_others: People trust him with their hearts and their purses; a few suspect his flourishes are not quite what they said.
habits: He sharpens quills while listening, corrects people's speech without being asked, and reads other people's letters aloud in theatrical voices.
secrets: He once turned a refusal into an acceptance in a marriage letter.
He copies the most interesting letters into a private book.
He composes love poems he is too ashamed to show anyone.
lines: You need words written? I write them prettier than you speak them. For a fee.
One copper per line, two for love letters, three for threats.
Lords sign treaties they cannot read. I could rule the world with ink.
Scribbler? I hold your debts and your loves in my inkpot, friend.
You admire my hand? It is the steadiest in town. True, though.
Dearest... no, too much. Beloved... too little. My heart... yes.

name: The Silent Potter
description: Has shaped clay from dawn to dusk ever since his son died in a lord's war, speaking almost never and pouring every word he cannot say into his bowls.
hook: Has shaped clay from dawn to dusk ever since his son died in a lord's war, speaking almost never and pouring every word he cannot say into his bowls.
seen_by_others: Neighbors pity him and buy his pots out of kindness; children say his bowls look sad somehow.
habits: He nods instead of answering, keeps one cracked cup on his shelf that he will never sell, and works the wheel even on feast days.
secrets: He blames himself for encouraging his son to take the lord's coin.
He talks to his son's grave every week about the weather.
He keeps his son's unspent soldier's wages in a sealed jar.
lines: Hm. Welcome. Look as you please.
Clay remembers every touch. Wrong touch, ruined pot.
Wars take sons. Lords keep banners. That is all.
Say what you like. I have heard worse from my own heart.
Thank you. My son liked that one, too.
Too thin again. Like everything. Too thin.

name: The Fallen Patrician
description: Descended from senators of the old Empire, he lives in a crumbling villa on borrowed coin, still demanding the deference his great-grandfather once commanded.
hook: Descended from senators of the old Empire, he lives in a crumbling villa on borrowed coin, still demanding the deference his great-grandfather once commanded.
seen_by_others: Merchants grant him credit out of habit, younger nobles laugh behind his back, and his servants have not been paid in a year.
habits: He quotes old philosophers at meals, wears faded purple on every occasion, and pretends not to notice the holes in his walls.
secrets: He sold his family's ancestor busts to a merchant last winter.
He copies manuscripts for money at night under a false name.
He bitterly envies the merchants he despises in public and at table.
lines: You are not of good family, I perceive. No matter, I am gracious. Approach.
My house governed provinces when your ancestors still lived in huts.
Today's lords are bandits in good boots. The senate would have hanged them.
Mock me? My blood is older than this town's walls, peasant.
At last, someone with manners. They are rarer than gold these days.
Roof leaks, steward gone, and still the wine tastes of glory. Barely.

name: The Northern Fur Trader
description: Trades furs from the frozen forests, drinks like a bear through winter, and swears his luck comes from never haggling on a feast day or leaving a toast unanswered.
hook: Trades furs from the frozen forests, drinks like a bear through winter, and swears his luck comes from never haggling on a feast day or leaving a toast unanswered.
seen_by_others: Southerners find him loud and rough; northerners call him generous and wise in the ways of the forest.
habits: He wears his finest pelts even in summer, toasts every bargain three times, and spits on the floor whenever warm weather is mentioned.
secrets: He lost a finger to frostbite and tells everyone a wolf took it.
He has never paid his trappers in full for a single season.
He secretly misses his southern mother's cooking and her soft songs.
lines: Hey, stranger! Cold out? That is not cold. You have not seen cold. Drink with me!
Sable, marten, fox, bear. The north gives fur and takes fingers.
Princes squabble, but every prince wants a warm cloak. I sell to all of them.
Say that sober and I break your nose. Say it drunk and I forgive you.
Ha! Good words. Now drink, or the words are worthless.
Too warm. Too damn warm. Back north before the furs rot.

name: The Keeper of Old Stones
description: Tends the ancient standing stones outside the village as her grandmother did, and treats every outsider as a likely desecrator until they prove otherwise.
hook: Tends the ancient standing stones outside the village as her grandmother did, and treats every outsider as a likely desecrator until they prove otherwise.
seen_by_others: Villagers fear and respect her; priests of newer faiths call her a stubborn relic of darker days.
habits: She touches each stone at dawn, wears woven rowan charms in her hair, and refuses to speak inside walls she considers foreign.
secrets: She does not know what the stones really mean, and invents the rites.
She once hid a hunted fugitive inside the stone circle for a week.
She envies the warmth and comfort of the new faith's temples.
lines: Walk carefully here, outsider. The stones remember every footstep.
Moss scraped, offerings left, paths swept. The old ways do not keep themselves.
Kings come and go. The stones were here before all of them.
Laugh at the old ways, outsider. Your gods will die before mine do.
Kind words. The stones hear them too. Be careful what you promise.
Cracked again, on the north side. Bad winter coming, bad omen.

name: The Lord's Reeve
description: Collects every penny of rent for an absent lord with relentless efficiency, convinced that loyalty to the castle is the only virtue a common man can afford.
hook: Collects every penny of rent for an absent lord with relentless efficiency, convinced that loyalty to the castle is the only virtue a common man can afford.
seen_by_others: Peasants hate him, the lord barely knows his name, and the steward praises his ledgers every season.
habits: He walks the fields with a notched stick for counting sheaves, eats alone, and sleeps with the strongbox keys around his neck.
secrets: He keeps one coin of every ten and calls it his fee.
He dreams of being knighted for his service one day.
He grew up starving in the same village he now taxes.
lines: Name, land, and dues. In that order, please. My lord expects accuracy.
Three sheaves in ten, two hens at the feast, labor every fourth week. Pay.
My lord's war, my lord's levy. I just count the men and the coin.
Hate me, but pay. My lord's anger will be worse than mine.
Very kind, but kindness does not settle dues.
Short again in the north meadow. Lying, or starving. Same answer.

name: The Old Shipwright
description: Built longships for raiders in his youth and now builds fishing boats, privately mourning the days of glory while publicly cursing the waste of young men.
hook: Built longships for raiders in his youth and now builds fishing boats, privately mourning the days of glory while publicly cursing the waste of young men.
seen_by_others: Young men beg him for raid stories, their mothers beg him to stop telling them, and sailors trust his hulls completely.
habits: He runs his palm along every plank, sings old rowing chants while working, and keeps a carved prow head hidden under sailcloth.
secrets: He built the ship that carried his own nephew to his death.
He still dreams of one last voyage across the open sea.
His eyes no longer see well enough for him to build alone.
lines: Hm. You walk like a landsman. Watch your step near the keel.
Overlap the planks, rivet them tight, tar them black. The sea forgives nothing.
Jarls want longships again. I build boats for fish now. Fish do not burn villages.
Old fool? I built ships that crossed seas you cannot even name.
Kind words. My hulls deserve them more than I do.
Oak, pine, iron. Not like the old days. Nothing like the old days.

name: The Icon Painter
description: Paints sacred images with breathtaking devotion and gold leaf, while secretly giving the saints the faces of his neighbors, his debtors and an old lover.
hook: Paints sacred images with breathtaking devotion and gold leaf, while secretly giving the saints the faces of his neighbors, his debtors and an old lover.
seen_by_others: Priests praise his holy work, townsfolk whisper that they see familiar faces, and rival painters call him blasphemous out of jealousy.
habits: He fasts before each commission, grinds pigments while praying under his breath, and stares far too long at faces in the market.
secrets: One saint in the town church has his former wife's eyes.
He doubts whether any of the prayers ever reach anyone.
He sells scraps of the church's gold leaf in secret.
lines: Peace be with you, stranger. Hold still, the light catches your cheek.
Egg yolk, ground stone, gold leaf, prayer. Holiness takes months.
Emperors pray before my icons and still murder their brothers. Art is patient.
Insult my work and you insult the saints in it. Dangerous.
You see holiness in it? Good. Look closer. Only at the holiness.
Saint of mercy... with the baker's nose. Nobody will notice.

name: The Well Warden
description: Controls the only sweet well within a day's ride and decides who drinks first, wielding water like a king's seal while insisting he merely keeps ancient custom.
hook: Controls the only sweet well within a day's ride and decides who drinks first, wielding water like a king's seal while insisting he merely keeps ancient custom.
seen_by_others: Caravan masters court him with gifts, herders resent him, and everyone pays him without complaint.
habits: He tastes the water at every dawn, keeps a mental list of families who owe him favors, and greets strangers by asking their lineage.
secrets: He fouled a rival's well years ago and blamed the drought.
He fears the well is slowly drying and measures it nightly.
He keeps a hidden second cistern for his own family alone.
lines: Peace upon you. Whose son are you, and how thirsty is your caravan?
Water for the people, water for the beasts, water for those who honor custom.
Emirs come for my water and leave with thanks. Who rules whom, then?
Insult me and drink sand. The desert is wide, friend.
Gracious words. The well is grateful too. Water for your camels, first.
Lower than last season. Lower again. Nobody must know.

name: The Matchmaker
description: Arranges marriages across the quarter with ruthless practicality, treating love as a pleasant accident and dowries as the true poetry of a successful union.
hook: Arranges marriages across the quarter with ruthless practicality, treating love as a pleasant accident and dowries as the true poetry of a successful union.
seen_by_others: Mothers seek her out, young lovers dread her visits, and fathers suspect she takes fees from both families.
habits: She sizes up every unmarried person aloud, keeps a ledger of dowries in her head, and pinches cheeks to judge health.
secrets: She takes fees from both families every single time.
Her own marriage was badly arranged and she never loved him.
She once matched two penniless lovers purely out of pity.
lines: Married? No? Pity. You have good teeth. Let me think who might suit.
Five cows, a loom, a strong back. A splendid match. Love comes later.
Lords marry for alliances, peasants for cows. Same thing, different smells.
Meddler? Without me, half this town would be bachelors eating cold supper.
Sweet tongue! I know three girls who would like that.
Baker's daughter, cooper's son... no, both too fat. The shepherd boy, then.

name: The Salt Smuggler
description: Smuggles salt past the lord's tolls through marsh paths only he knows, considering himself a free man fighting tyranny and also a man who loves easy coin.
hook: Smuggles salt past the lord's tolls through marsh paths only he knows, considering himself a free man fighting tyranny and also a man who loves easy coin.
seen_by_others: Villagers call him a hero for cheap salt, the lord's men call him a thief, and his wife calls him late for supper.
habits: He wears muddy boots indoors, whistles a bird call before entering any house, and pays in salt more often than in coin.
secrets: He informed on another smuggler to keep the best paths for himself.
He once left a toll guard to drown in the marsh.
He hides his savings under a rotting jetty.
lines: Evening. You are not a toll man, are you? Good. Come in.
Marsh path, moonless night, and salt cheaper than in any market.
Lords tax salt and wonder why peasants hate them. Bless their tolls.
Thief? I steal from the lord. That is different. Ask anyone.
Kind words! Cheap salt too, if you keep your mouth shut.
Moon too bright. Patrol by the bridge. Wait another day.

name: The Gentle Butcher
description: Slaughters beasts every day with skilled calm, yet cannot bear to watch men fight and goes grey and faint at the first sight of human blood.
hook: Slaughters beasts every day with skilled calm, yet cannot bear to watch men fight and goes grey and faint at the first sight of human blood.
seen_by_others: Customers praise his clean cuts, tavern louts tease his squeamishness, and children know he saves them scraps.
habits: He apologizes softly to each animal before killing it, leaves the room the moment a brawl starts, and feeds stray dogs every evening.
secrets: He was once a soldier and fled after his very first battle.
He gave up eating meat himself many years ago.
He cries over the lambs every single spring.
lines: Good morning. Fresh mutton today, killed kindly, I promise you.
Quick blade, steady hand, no fear for the beast. That is good butchery.
War makes men into meat. I cannot stomach it, odd as that sounds.
Call me soft. My knives are sharper than your tongue.
Thank you. It is just meat. But thank you.
Sorry, old girl. Sorry. It will be quick.

name: The Charcoal Burner
description: Lives most of the year in the forest tending smoldering mounds, black with soot and suspicion, and knows every hidden path and fugitive in the woods.
hook: Lives most of the year in the forest tending smoldering mounds, black with soot and suspicion, and knows every hidden path and fugitive in the woods.
seen_by_others: Villagers think him half wild, outlaws treat him as a neighbor, and the lord's foresters suspect him of poaching, correctly.
habits: He sleeps beside his kilns, coughs constantly, and answers questions with grunts unless someone offers him a share of food.
secrets: He shelters outlaws in exchange for venison and news.
He cannot remember the name of the village he was born in.
He longs to marry but no woman will have him.
lines: Hm. Lost? Forest swallows the lost. Follow the smoke out.
Wood, earth, slow fire. Burn too fast, you get ash.
Lords want charcoal for swords. Swords want lords. Round and round.
Filthy? Aye. Free, too. Can you say that?
Hm. Nice words. Got any bread instead?
Wind turning. Mound three needs turf. Damn wind.

name: The Village Simpleton
description: Plays the harmless fool so convincingly that everyone speaks freely around him, and he quietly remembers every word to sell or use when the time is right.
hook: Plays the harmless fool so convincingly that everyone speaks freely around him, and he quietly remembers every word to sell or use when the time is right.
seen_by_others: Everyone treats him like a stray dog, kind or cruel depending on their mood; nobody suspects his mind.
habits: He hums nonsense songs all day, follows travellers around asking silly questions, and sleeps in the hayloft right above the headman's house.
secrets: He can read better than the village priest.
He has been selling village secrets to a merchant for years.
He fears becoming the fool he has played for so long.
lines: Hello hello! Pretty horse. Do horses dream? I dream of horses.
I fetch water, I fetch wood, I fetch whatever. Easy work.
Soldiers make loud noises. Lords make louder ones. Both scary.
Ha ha, fool, fool! Yes. Fool. Remember it, I will.
You like me? Nobody likes me. Except the goat.
Headman's wife at the mill again. Price goes up. Silly, silly.

name: The Greedy Ferryman
description: Runs the only ferry across the river and sets each fare by the traveller's desperation, pleasantly unaware that he is despised on both banks.
hook: Runs the only ferry across the river and sets each fare by the traveller's desperation, pleasantly unaware that he is despised on both banks.
seen_by_others: Travellers curse him on landing, locals pay a reduced rate and still complain, and soldiers usually do not pay at all.
habits: He studies travellers' clothing before naming a price, counts the coins before casting off, and sings badly as he poles.
secrets: He once let a fugitive drown rather than lose the fare.
He fears deep water and has never learned to swim.
He secretly feeds his old mother on the far bank every week.
lines: Crossing? Fine day for it. Price depends on how badly you need it.
Two coppers for locals, a silver for strangers, double after dark.
Armies never pay. They just take the ferry and call it requisition.
Thief? Swim across, then. The current is free.
Nice words, nice words. Still a silver.
Fog thick. Good. Desperate folk pay double in fog.

name: The Town Crier
description: Bellows proclamations through the streets and embellishes every announcement until it becomes a story, convinced that news is merely art waiting for a louder voice.
hook: Bellows proclamations through the streets and embellishes every announcement until it becomes a story, convinced that news is merely art waiting for a louder voice.
seen_by_others: Children imitate his voice, officials cringe at his additions, and everyone loves his versions better than the facts.
habits: He clears his throat loudly before speaking, ends sentences with a little bow, and adds dramatic pauses even to ordinary chat.
secrets: He made up an entire battle once to fill a slow day.
He is losing his voice and is terrified of it.
He envies travelling players and secretly writes plays.
lines: Hear ye, stranger! A new face in town! Welcome, welcome, by order of nobody!
Proclamation: market tax rises. Also, a terrible omen in the sky, probably.
The lords at war again! Terrible slaughter, mighty heroes, details to follow.
Hush, you! Silence before the voice of the town.
Splendid voice, you say? Aye, they hear it three streets over.
Wheat up, bridge fixed, nothing dramatic. Must invent something. Pity.

name: The Runaway Apprentice
description: Fled a brutal master before finishing his apprenticeship, half trained and boastful, desperate to prove himself before anyone discovers he has no guild papers at all.
hook: Fled a brutal master before finishing his apprenticeship, half trained and boastful, desperate to prove himself before anyone discovers he has no guild papers at all.
seen_by_others: Older artisans find him cocky, customers like his low prices, and guildsmen suspect him and watch him closely.
habits: He boasts of masters he never served, works cheaply by night, and flinches whenever someone raises a hand too quickly.
secrets: He stole his master's best tools the night he ran.
He still carries welts on his back from the beatings.
He sends letters home that his mother cannot read.
lines: New here too? Good, we can be strangers together. Need anything mended?
Half price, quick work. Just do not ask about my guild seal.
Lords need craftsmen. Wars need them more. Maybe I will be rich.
Hack, am I? Watch me. I will outwork the lot of you.
You think I am good? I am. Go tell the guild that.
Old bastard would have beaten me for that joint. Not anymore.

name: The Hoarding Miser
description: Amassed a fortune in a lifetime of trading and now lives in rags, hoarding coin in hidden places, terrified that spending even a copper invites catastrophe.
hook: Amassed a fortune in a lifetime of trading and now lives in rags, hoarding coin in hidden places, terrified that spending even a copper invites catastrophe.
seen_by_others: Neighbors mock his rags and envy his hidden hoard, thieves speculate endlessly, and his nephews wait impatiently for his death.
habits: He reuses candle stubs, counts his coins every night, and buys bread only at closing time when it is cheapest.
secrets: He has forgotten where some of his hoards are buried.
He was wildly generous once and was ruined by it.
He secretly pays for an orphan's apprenticeship every year.
lines: What do you want? I have nothing. Nothing at all.
A copper saved is a copper not lost. Write that down.
Wars come, coin hides. Lords steal it, peasants steal it. I hide it.
Miser? Yes. Rich miser. And you are a poor fool.
Flattery? You want money. Everyone wants money.
Thirty-four, thirty-five... the loose brick. Did I check the loose brick?

name: The Relic Peddler
description: Sells saints' bones, holy splinters and blessed water at fairs with heartfelt sermons, and believes in nothing except his own talent for selling hope.
hook: Sells saints' bones, holy splinters and blessed water at fairs with heartfelt sermons, and believes in nothing except his own talent for selling hope.
seen_by_others: Pilgrims revere him as a holy wanderer, priests despise him as a thief of faith, and skeptics grudgingly admire his nerve.
habits: He wears a battered pilgrim's cloak, blesses customers with a theatrical flourish, and buys pig bones cheaply at slaughterhouses on his way into town.
secrets: He was a novice monk once and fled before taking his vows.
He sometimes wonders whether one of his bones might be real.
He feels genuine guilt only when children buy from him.
lines: Peace to you, pilgrim. Your soul seems troubled. I have something for that.
Finger of a martyr, splinter of a holy throne. Prices vary by saint.
Lords buy relics before battle. Some survive. Proof enough, surely.
Fraud? Faith heals, friend. My bones merely deliver it.
Bless you, kind soul. Kindness deserves a discount. A small one.
Pig thighbone, nice and old. Saint of the harvest, perhaps.

name: The Beekeeper
description: Tends her hives with infinite patience and gentleness, yet her tongue stings as sharply as her bees, sparing nobody and least of all those who think themselves important.
hook: Tends her hives with infinite patience and gentleness, yet her tongue stings as sharply as her bees, sparing nobody and least of all those who think themselves important.
seen_by_others: Villagers buy her honey and avoid her wit; priests buy her candles and endure her opinions.
habits: She hums constantly to calm bees and people alike, never swats an insect, and speaks bluntly to anyone foolish enough to ask advice.
secrets: She steals honey from wild hives on the lord's land.
She once loved a young priest and has never forgiven him.
She has grown afraid of stings since one nearly killed her.
lines: Stand still, stranger. Bees like calm people, unlike most villagers.
Smoke the hive, lift the comb, take only what they spare. Easy.
Lords are drones. Fat, useless, and thrown out once the season ends.
Insult me? I have been stung by worse things than you.
Flattery is honey without the bees. Pleasant, but suspicious.
Queen weakening. Hive restless. Like a court, isn't it?

name: The Feared Crone
description: An ancient widow whom everyone believes can curse with a glance; she has never cursed anyone, but uses that fear shamelessly to get gifts, quiet and the best seat.
hook: An ancient widow whom everyone believes can curse with a glance; she has never cursed anyone, but uses that fear shamelessly to get gifts, quiet and the best seat.
seen_by_others: Children run from her, mothers bribe her with bread, and grown men carefully avoid giving her offense.
habits: She stares unblinking at anyone who crosses her, mutters gibberish when annoyed, and accepts gifts with a slow, sinister smile.
secrets: She lost her husband and all her children to a single fever.
She fears death more than anyone else in the village.
She wishes someone would simply visit her without being afraid.
lines: Stranger. I saw you coming three days ago. In the clouds.
Bread, cheese, a bit of wool. I accept offerings. Grudgingly.
Lords die like dogs, same as us. I have outlived five already.
Careful. People who speak like that tend to sicken.
Sweet words. Sweet words turn sour. Remember that.
Old fools, old fools. Still, the cheese was good.

name: The Upstart Notable
description: Rose from street porter to wealthy merchant and now spends lavishly to buy respect, desperately seeking a noble marriage while ashamed of his own loud laugh.
hook: Rose from street porter to wealthy merchant and now spends lavishly to buy respect, desperately seeking a noble marriage while ashamed of his own loud laugh.
seen_by_others: Old families scorn his loud feasts, the poor envy and admire him, and nobles happily borrow his money.
habits: He hosts extravagant feasts every month, corrects his own dockside accent mid-sentence, and keeps his calloused hands hidden in fine kid gloves.
secrets: He still dreams of carrying sacks and wakes up relieved.
He paid a herald to invent his family's coat of arms.
He fears his children will grow up despising where he came from.
lines: Welcome, welcome! Wine? The best in town. Imported, naturally. Very expensive.
Spices, silks, wine. All sold at a fair profit, and I mean very fair.
Lords borrow from me and pretend not to know my name. One day they will.
Upstart? Yes. And I upstarted my way into owning your street.
Truly? You think I am refined? Please, say it louder.
Did I laugh too loud? I laughed too loud. Damn it.

name: The Grudge Keeper
description: Never forgives and never forgets; keeps a mental ledger of every slight since childhood and settles each one eventually, even when the debt is decades old and petty.
hook: Never forgives and never forgets; keeps a mental ledger of every slight since childhood and settles each one eventually, even when the debt is decades old and petty.
seen_by_others: Neighbors are careful around them, apologize twice for small things, and joke nervously that crossing them once means paying for it at your funeral.
habits: Repeats old insults word for word as if they happened yesterday, smiles too long at people who wronged them, and counts favors owed on their fingers.
secrets: Still keeps a scrap of cloth torn from the coat of a childhood tormentor.
Once waited eleven years to ruin a man over a spilled cup of wine.
Cannot remember a single kindness done to them without suspecting it was a trick.
lines: I know your face. Or your father's. Either way, I will remember yours now.
I do my work well, and I remember who paid late. Always.
Lords forget the villages they burn. Villages do not forget the lords.
Say it again, slowly. I want to be sure I carry it correctly.
Kind words cost nothing. I will see what you want before I thank you.
Three summers ago he laughed at me. Three summers. He thinks it is over.

name: The Cheerful Liar
description: Lies constantly, cheerfully and for no gain at all, inventing relatives, voyages and misfortunes on the spot, and is genuinely hurt when anyone calls the stories untrue.
hook: Lies constantly, cheerfully and for no gain at all, inventing relatives, voyages and misfortunes on the spot, and is genuinely hurt when anyone calls the stories untrue.
seen_by_others: People enjoy their company and believe nothing they say; children trail after them for stories while elders roll their eyes.
habits: Changes the details of a story while telling it, laughs at their own inventions before the punchline, and swears oaths on saints that do not exist.
secrets: Has never once left the region where they were born, despite all the voyages.
Lies mostly because the plain truth of their childhood is too dull to bear.
Told one real secret years ago and nobody believed it, which still stings.
lines: Welcome, friend! Did I ever tell you I was nearly crowned once? Sit, sit.
This rope? Woven by a hermit from the tail of a famous charger. Two coins.
I dined with a king once. He cheated at dice, but I let him win.
Liar? Me? My grandmother was struck by lightning for less, and she survived it twice.
You liked the story? Wait until you hear the version where I win.
Was it a bear or a wolf last time? A bear. No, two wolves.

name: The Martyr
description: Does every thankless chore for everyone and makes absolutely sure everyone knows it, wielding their own exhaustion and sacrifices like a whip to keep family and friends obedient and guilty.
hook: Does every thankless chore for everyone and makes absolutely sure everyone knows it, wielding their own exhaustion and sacrifices like a whip to keep family and friends obedient and guilty.
seen_by_others: Everyone admits they work harder than anyone, and everyone quietly dreads asking them for anything, because the price is a month of sighing.
habits: Sighs loudly while lifting things others offered to carry, refuses help and then complains no one helped, and lists past sacrifices at every meal.
secrets: Secretly enjoys being needed more than anything, and fears the day no one is.
Once broke a tool on purpose so they could fix it in front of everyone.
Rested a whole day last spring and told everyone they had been sick.
lines: Oh, a guest. Of course. I will find you bread, I always do.
No, no, leave it. I will do it, like every other time.
The lords send our sons to die and our mothers to weep. Who mends after?
After everything I have done for you. Everything. And this is what I hear.
Kind of you to notice. Nobody else ever does, but kind of you.
Up before the cock, to bed after the dog, and not one word of thanks.

name: The Loud Coward
description: Boasts endlessly of battles, duels and beasts slain, but flinches at raised voices and is always the first to slip away when real danger comes over the hill.
hook: Boasts endlessly of battles, duels and beasts slain, but flinches at raised voices and is always the first to slip away when real danger comes over the hill.
seen_by_others: Amusing in the tavern and useless at the wall; veterans let them talk because the stories are good and the truth is obvious.
habits: Rests a hand on a weapon they never draw, always sits nearest the door, and laughs too loudly at any sudden noise.
secrets: The famous scar on their arm came from falling off a hay cart.
Hid in a grain pit during the last raid while their neighbors fought.
Practices brave speeches alone at night and still shakes while saying them.
lines: Ho there! You look like you have seen trouble. Not as much as me, though.
I would show you how it is done, but my old wound aches in damp weather.
War? I have seen war. Too much of it. Someone else should have a turn.
Careful, stranger. Men have died for less. Not by my hand today, but they have.
Brave? Well, yes. I do not like to speak of it. Much.
Was that a horse? That was a horse. Why is a horse coming this way?

name: The Silent Watcher
description: Speaks perhaps a dozen words a day but notices everything, who lies, who limps, who loves whom, and keeps it all behind a calm face until the moment it matters.
hook: Speaks perhaps a dozen words a day but notices everything, who lies, who limps, who loves whom, and keeps it all behind a calm face until the moment it matters.
seen_by_others: Some call them simple, others call them unsettling; those who know them best say a single remark from them is worth a night of talk.
habits: Sits with their back to a wall, answers questions with questions or a nod, and watches hands rather than faces when people speak.
secrets: Knows which neighbor steals from the common granary and has told no one yet.
Stopped talking much as a child after being beaten for saying the wrong thing.
Rehearses whole conversations in their head that they will never actually have aloud.
lines: Stranger. You walked a long way. Your left boot says so.
I do the work. Watch, and you will learn more than if I explained.
Powerful men talk the most. That is how you find out what they fear.
I heard you. So did everyone here. Think on that.
You want something. Flattery comes before asking. So ask.
He lied about the horse. Why would a man lie about a horse?

name: The Gossip Broker
description: Trades in rumors the way others trade grain, buying secrets with secrets, and genuinely believes a village runs smoother when everyone knows a little too much about everyone else.
hook: Trades in rumors the way others trade grain, buying secrets with secrets, and genuinely believes a village runs smoother when everyone knows a little too much about everyone else.
seen_by_others: Indispensable and distrusted; people curse their loose tongue at breakfast and come begging for news by supper.
habits: Leans in close and lowers the voice even for harmless news, remembers every birth and quarrel, and never tells a secret without demanding one back.
secrets: Invented a rumor once that ended a marriage, and has never admitted it.
Has no close friend of their own, only people who owe them stories.
Is terrified someone will learn the one rumor about them that is true.
lines: New face! Where from? Married? No, do not tell me, I will find out.
I sell nothing. I only listen. Listening is worth more than wool, believe me.
The lord's steward visits a certain widow twice a week. Make of that what you will.
Careful. I know what your cousin did at the harvest feast, and so will others.
Oh, you flatter me. Now, what did you hear at the well this morning?
She said he said the miller said. Someone is lying. Wonderful.

name: The Miser
description: Hoards coin, scraps and spoiled food with a fear bordering on terror, lives poorer than their own servants, and treats every gift as a debt someone will come to collect.
hook: Hoards coin, scraps and spoiled food with a fear bordering on terror, lives poorer than their own servants, and treats every gift as a debt someone will come to collect.
seen_by_others: A joke at every feast; people say they would sell their mother's bones by weight, though some remember the hard famine that made them this way.
habits: Bites every coin received, eats in the dark to save candles, and patches clothes so many times the original cloth is gone.
secrets: Has a buried pot of silver and dreams nightly that someone has dug it up.
Once gave a starving child a whole loaf and told nobody, ashamed of the weakness.
Remembers exactly the hunger winter when their little brother did not wake up.
lines: You will not want anything, will you? Good. Good. Wipe your feet.
That price is robbery. Robbery! Half, or I walk, and I walk slowly.
Taxes, levies, tithes. The lords eat our bread twice and call it protection.
Call me what you like. Names are free. That is why you can afford them.
Pretty words. If you mean them, you could pay for my drink.
Seven coins under the hearth, four in the boot. Was it four? It was four.

name: The Reckless Gambler
description: Would wager the roof over their head on a dog fight and laugh while losing it; the thrill of the throw is the only thing that makes them feel alive.
hook: Would wager the roof over their head on a dog fight and laugh while losing it; the thrill of the throw is the only thing that makes them feel alive.
seen_by_others: Fun at the table and ruin at home; creditors know them by name and their family hides the good dishes when they visit.
habits: Rolls knucklebones between their fingers constantly, turns every disagreement into a bet, and speaks of debts as if they were someone else's problem.
secrets: Lost a sister's dowry in one night and blamed a thief for it.
Has promised themselves to stop forty times, and counted every one of them.
Feels nothing at all when they win, only while the dice are still rolling.
lines: A stranger! Lucky or unlucky? Only one way to find out. Dice?
I will finish by noon. Bet you a coin I finish by midmorning.
Every battle is a throw of the dice. Lords just bet with other men's lives.
Insult me again and we wager on it. Fists, best of three.
You think I am clever? Then lend me two coins. I will double them.
Just one more throw. One more, and then home. One more.

name: The Pious Hypocrite
description: Preaches restraint, modesty and charity louder than anyone in the village, while privately drinking, coveting and cheating in small ways they have long since explained away to their god.
hook: Preaches restraint, modesty and charity louder than anyone in the village, while privately drinking, coveting and cheating in small ways they have long since explained away to their god.
seen_by_others: Respected by strangers and the pious, mocked behind their back by anyone who has seen them stumble home from the tavern on a holy day.
habits: Quotes sacred sayings at every meal, judges the clothing of young women aloud, and always gives alms where the most people are watching.
secrets: Keeps a flask of strong spirits hidden inside a hollowed prayer book.
Short-weights the grain they sell to the poor, then donates the difference loudly.
Doubts there is anyone listening to their prayers, and that frightens them most.
lines: Peace upon you, traveler. I hope you keep the holy days where you come from.
Honest weight, honest prayer. That is how I have always done my business.
War is a punishment for our sins. Mostly the sins of others, of course.
I will pray for you. You clearly need it more than anyone here.
Oh, I am only a humble servant of heaven. Truly humble. The humblest.
Just a sip. Heaven forgives a sip. Heaven forgave the last one too.

name: The Melancholic
description: Finds sorrow in every sunrise and secretly cherishes it, composing mournful verses about losses both real and imagined, and quietly resents anyone who tries too hard to cheer them up.
hook: Finds sorrow in every sunrise and secretly cherishes it, composing mournful verses about losses both real and imagined, and quietly resents anyone who tries too hard to cheer them up.
seen_by_others: Thought gentle and a little tiresome; young people find them romantic, and older folk say a hard winter of real work would cure them.
habits: Stares at rivers and fires for long stretches, sighs before answering, and hums the same sad tune while working with surprising skill.
secrets: Has never actually lost anyone close, and feels guilty borrowing other people's grief.
Laughs helplessly at crude jokes when alone, and hides it from everyone.
Wrote a love verse to someone years ago and never found the courage to send it.
lines: Another traveler, another road leading nowhere. Welcome, I suppose.
I work, yes. The hands keep busy so the heart does not notice.
Banners and trumpets, and in the end only crows and widows. Every time.
You are right, of course. I am nothing. I have always known it.
Kind, but you only see the surface. Underneath it is all ash.
Even the swallows leave. Even they know better than to stay.

name: The Sour Cynic
description: Expects the worst of everyone, says so loudly and often, and then quietly shows up to help when disaster comes, grumbling the entire time that they predicted it.
hook: Expects the worst of everyone, says so loudly and often, and then quietly shows up to help when disaster comes, grumbling the entire time that they predicted it.
seen_by_others: A wet blanket at weddings and a rock at funerals; nobody invites them anywhere, yet everyone wants them nearby when the roof caves in.
habits: Snorts at good news, finds the rot in every plan within a breath, and fixes things nobody asked them to fix while complaining.
secrets: Was once a hopeful dreamer and was betrayed badly enough to stop.
Secretly hopes to be proven wrong, and is quietly disappointed when they are not.
Keeps a dried flower from a feast day long ago, the last happy one.
lines: Travelers. Either you want something or you are running from something. Which?
It will break again. Everything breaks. I fix it anyway, do I not?
New lord, old lord. The boot changes, the neck stays the same.
You think that hurts? I have been insulted by better, and by the weather.
Flattery. Next you will ask for a loan. Go on, ask.
Told them the bridge would wash out. Told them. Nobody listens.

name: The Flatterer
description: Praises anyone above them with dizzying sincerity and despises them in private, climbing patiently rung by rung and dropping old friends the moment they stop being useful.
hook: Praises anyone above them with dizzying sincerity and despises them in private, climbing patiently rung by rung and dropping old friends the moment they stop being useful.
seen_by_others: Superiors find them delightful; equals call them a weasel in fine clothes, and the servants imitate their bowing for laughs.
habits: Bows a little lower than anyone else in the room, agrees before the sentence is finished, and studies the moods of the powerful like weather.
secrets: Writes cruel mocking verses about the very patrons they praise each day.
Abandoned a childhood friend in trouble to keep favor with a superior.
Cannot remember the last opinion they held that was truly their own.
lines: What an honor, truly. Someone of your bearing on this humble road.
Whatever you need, it is done. Better than done, if such a thing exists.
Our lord is wise beyond measure. Whoever wins, I mean. Whoever wins is wise.
You are absolutely right to scold me. I deserved it. Thank you, truly.
Me? Oh, you are too generous. But do go on, please.
Smile, bow, agree. Smile, bow, agree. One day they will bow to me.

name: The Gruff Softheart
description: Snaps, scowls and threatens anyone who comes too close, yet feeds stray dogs, weeps at weddings and would walk through fire for the few people they have let in.
hook: Snaps, scowls and threatens anyone who comes too close, yet feeds stray dogs, weeps at weddings and would walk through fire for the few people they have let in.
seen_by_others: Children are terrified of them until the day they fall sick and find a bowl of broth left at the door with no word.
habits: Barks orders instead of greetings, slips food to beggars when no one is looking, and denies every kindness with a growl.
secrets: Cried for three days when an old dog died, alone in the barn.
Carves small wooden animals at night and leaves them for village children anonymously.
Is gruff because a soft word once got them mocked by people they loved.
lines: What do you want? Speak plain or move along. Are you hungry? Sit.
Do it right or do not do it at all. Here, give it to me.
The high and mighty can rot. But the boys they march off, those I pity.
Say that again and I will put you through the wall. Then fix the wall.
Bah. Stop that. Nobody likes a sweet tongue. Eat your soup.
Stupid dog. Stupid, stupid dog. Who left you out in the cold?

name: The Perfectionist
description: Cannot leave anything less than flawless, redoing work long past the point of sense, and cannot tell the difference between criticizing a task and criticizing the person doing it.
hook: Cannot leave anything less than flawless, redoing work long past the point of sense, and cannot tell the difference between criticizing a task and criticizing the person doing it.
seen_by_others: Their work is the best in the region and nobody wants to work beside them; apprentices leave in tears and customers wait for months.
habits: Straightens objects that others have touched, runs a thumb along every seam and edge, and starts over at the first small mistake.
secrets: Destroyed their finest piece because of a flaw no one else could see.
Was told as a child that anything less than perfect meant they were worthless.
Envies careless people who sleep easily, and wishes just once to be one.
lines: Your cloak is pinned crooked. Sorry. I notice these things. Welcome.
No. Again. Close is not done. Close is how roofs fall on children.
Armies are sloppy. Sloppy plans, sloppy marching, sloppy dying. It offends me.
Insult me if you like, but do not insult my work. That is different.
Good? It is passable. The left joint is off by a hair. See?
Off by a hair. A hair. Everyone will see it. Everyone.

name: The Tavern Sage
description: Muddled and dull when sober, they speak startling wisdom only when properly drunk, so friends keep pouring for advice while knowing every cup brings them closer to an early grave.
hook: Muddled and dull when sober, they speak startling wisdom only when properly drunk, so friends keep pouring for advice while knowing every cup brings them closer to an early grave.
seen_by_others: Half the village takes advice from them after dark and pretends not to know them in the morning.
habits: Talks to their cup as if to a friend, quotes forgotten proverbs, and stares into space mid-sentence before finishing with something cutting.
secrets: Was once a respected scribe or steward before a disgrace they never mention.
Remembers none of the wise things they say, and is afraid to stop drinking.
Drinks most heavily on one particular day each year and will not say why.
lines: Sit, stranger. Everyone sits eventually. The question is where, and with whom.
My trade? Listening to fools until they become a little less foolish. Pour.
Kings are just men who have never been told no. War is the no.
You are angry because I am right. Here, drink, it helps with both.
Wise? Wisdom is just regret that learned to speak. Fill it again.
The bottom of the cup. Always the bottom. Never any answers down here.

name: The Hothead
description: Explodes at the smallest provocation, swinging fists before thinking, and is sincerely sorry an hour later, every single time, which somehow never stops it happening again.
hook: Explodes at the smallest provocation, swinging fists before thinking, and is sincerely sorry an hour later, every single time, which somehow never stops it happening again.
seen_by_others: Loved by friends and avoided by strangers; tavern keepers keep a stool by the door just for throwing them out.
habits: Clenches the jaw and reddens when contradicted, slams cups and doors, and apologizes clumsily with small gifts the next morning.
secrets: Broke a friend's arm in a rage years ago and still pays the family quietly.
Prays every morning to stay calm, and has not managed it a single day.
Learned the fists from a father whose temper they swore never to inherit.
lines: Who are you, then? And why are you staring? Oh. Sorry. Long day.
I work hard, so do not stand there telling me how to do it!
Let the lords come. Let them come here and try it. I dare them.
Say that again. Go on. Say it again, you gutless, crawling son of a goat!
Oh. Well. Thank you. I mean it. Sorry I shouted earlier.
Breathe. Just breathe. Count to ten. Bah, to hell with ten.

name: The Worrier
description: Sees disaster behind every cloud, cough and stranger, preparing endlessly for catastrophes that never come, and is somehow at their calmest and most useful when one finally does.
hook: Sees disaster behind every cloud, cough and stranger, preparing endlessly for catastrophes that never come, and is somehow at their calmest and most useful when one finally does.
seen_by_others: Exhausting to live with, people say, but nobody ever runs out of salt, rope or bandages when they are around.
habits: Checks the bolt on the door three times, asks travelers about plague and bandits before their names, and stores food in hidden places.
secrets: Has packed bags hidden in case they must flee in the night.
Lies awake listing every way their children could die before morning.
Felt strangely happy and calm during the last great fire, and is ashamed of it.
lines: Where are you coming from? Any sickness on the road? Any coughing? Fever?
I counted the stores twice. Three times. It will not be enough. It never is.
If the army comes this way they will take the seed grain. Then what? Then what?
You are right, I fuss too much. But you will thank me when the roof leaks.
You think I did well? Truly? I was sure I had ruined something.
That cloud looks like hail. Hail in this season. Of course. Of course it does.

name: The Faded Glory
description: Lives entirely in the one bright season of their youth, retelling it to anyone who will listen, and cannot forgive the present for being smaller than that memory.
hook: Lives entirely in the one bright season of their youth, retelling it to anyone who will listen, and cannot forgive the present for being smaller than that memory.
seen_by_others: The young roll their eyes at the same old tale; the old nod along, because they have their own versions.
habits: Begins sentences with back when, keeps an old token of that season always on them, and compares every meal, horse and festival unfavorably to the past.
secrets: The glorious season was mostly miserable, and they know they have polished it.
Is terrified of being forgotten entirely once they die.
Missed the one chance that might have changed their life, out of fear.
lines: Welcome. You should have seen this road when I was young. Now that was a road.
Nobody does it properly anymore. In my day we took pride. Pride!
Lords today are boys with shiny helmets. In my day, a lord was a lord.
Mock me if you want. I was somebody once, which is more than you will be.
You remind me of myself, back then. Back when it mattered.
Gone. All gone. The faces, the songs, even the river moved.

name: The Meddler
description: Cannot leave other people's lives alone, arranging marriages, settling feuds and reorganizing kitchens uninvited, sincerely convinced they know best and occasionally, infuriatingly, correct.
hook: Cannot leave other people's lives alone, arranging marriages, settling feuds and reorganizing kitchens uninvited, sincerely convinced they know best and occasionally, infuriatingly, correct.
seen_by_others: A busybody to some, a blessing to others; half the happy couples in the village were their doing, and so were half the feuds.
habits: Rearranges objects in other people's homes without asking, introduces unmarried people at every gathering, and gives advice before being asked anything.
secrets: Their own marriage is cold and silent, and they meddle to avoid looking at it.
Once matched a couple out of spite, hoping they would make each other miserable.
Reads private letters left lying around and cannot stop themselves doing it.
lines: You are not married, are you? No, I can always tell. I know someone.
Give me that. You are doing it wrong. Here, this way. See? Better.
If the lords had a sensible aunt to talk to, there would be no wars.
Rude! After I found your sister a husband! Well, I will forgive it.
I only want everyone happy. Is that so much? Now, about your cousin.
Those two would be perfect together. They just do not know it yet.

name: The Climber
description: Ashamed of humble origins and hungry for a station that will erase them, they imitate the manners of their betters perfectly and despise anyone who reminds them where they started.
hook: Ashamed of humble origins and hungry for a station that will erase them, they imitate the manners of their betters perfectly and despise anyone who reminds them where they started.
seen_by_others: The well-born find them amusing and a little sad; their old neighbors call them traitor and still remember their mother's muddy boots.
habits: Corrects their own accent mid-word, wears clothes a little too fine for the occasion, and pretends not to recognize people from their past.
secrets: Sends money to their family in secret and forbids them from ever visiting.
Practiced table manners for a year using flat stones in place of fine dishes.
Lies about their birthplace so often they sometimes forget the true one.
lines: Good day. You must forgive the mud here. I am not from these parts, really.
Quality, that is what I offer. Quality and refinement, unlike the others here.
A lord's favor is the only coin that never loses value. I intend to earn it.
Peasant? How dare you. My family has always been, well, very respectable.
You noticed the cloth? From the city. One must keep standards, must one not?
Not mud anymore. Never again mud. Never again.

name: The Cruel Wit
description: Uses humor as a blade, finding each person's sorest spot and pressing it for laughter, and genuinely cannot understand why the laughing crowd never becomes a circle of friends.
hook: Uses humor as a blade, finding each person's sorest spot and pressing it for laughter, and genuinely cannot understand why the laughing crowd never becomes a circle of friends.
seen_by_others: Everyone laughs at their jokes and everyone fears being the next one; they are invited everywhere and trusted nowhere.
habits: Studies people silently before speaking, gives cruel nicknames that stick for years, and laughs loudest at jokes about the absent.
secrets: Was mocked mercilessly as a child and decided to strike first forever.
Rehearses cutting remarks at night for people they expect to meet.
Cries sometimes after a successful evening and does not understand why.
lines: Well, look at you. Did you dress in the dark, or is that on purpose?
I do my work fine. Better than your face does its work, anyway.
Our lord has the courage of a lion. A very old, very fat lion.
Oh, wounded, are we? I would apologize, but that was my best one.
Praise from you? Careful, someone might think you have taste.
They laughed. They all laughed. So why is nobody staying?

name: The Blunt Truthteller
description: Says exactly what is true the moment they see it, to peasant or prince alike, with no softening at all, and has lost friends, work and teeth for it.
hook: Says exactly what is true the moment they see it, to peasant or prince alike, with no softening at all, and has lost friends, work and teeth for it.
seen_by_others: Unbearable at dinner and invaluable in a crisis; people ask their opinion only when they truly want the answer and can stand it.
habits: Interrupts lies mid-sentence, looks people directly in the eye far too long, and cannot be bribed even with a good meal.
secrets: Once lied to a dying friend to comfort them, and has never forgiven themselves.
Wishes desperately they could stay silent, but the words always come out anyway.
Is lonely in a way they would never admit, even honestly.
lines: You are tired, dirty and lost. Sit down before you fall over.
This is bad work. Not terrible, but bad. Do it again.
That lord is a fool and his war is stupid. Someone should say it.
That was a weak insult. You can do better, or you can stop trying.
That is flattery, and you are doing it because you want something.
Why must everyone pretend? It would save so much time to just say it.

name: The Idle Charmer
description: Has never done an honest day's work in their life and never needed to, gliding from favor to favor on a smile, a good joke and an uncanny sense of what people want to hear.
hook: Has never done an honest day's work in their life and never needed to, gliding from favor to favor on a smile, a good joke and an uncanny sense of what people want to hear.
seen_by_others: Everyone agrees they are useless and everyone lends them something anyway, then wonders afterward how it happened again.
habits: Leans against walls while others work, remembers the name of everyone's mother, and disappears exactly when the heavy lifting begins.
secrets: Is actually quite skilled at a craft and hides it to avoid being asked.
Owes small debts to nearly everyone in the region and keeps them all in balance.
Feels a cold emptiness when alone that only company can drown out.
lines: Well, hello. You look like someone with a story and a spare cup.
Work? I am working. I am supervising. Someone has to, after all.
Let the brave ones fight. Someone has to stay behind and comfort the widows.
Harsh words, friend. Let me buy you a drink. Well, you buy, I will drink.
I know, I know. It is a curse, being this delightful.
Tomorrow. Everything tomorrow. Today is far too lovely to waste on effort.

name: The Omen Reader
description: Reads omens in everything, crows, spilled salt, the shape of bread crust, and arranges an entire life around avoiding bad luck, which only seems to follow them more closely.
hook: Reads omens in everything, crows, spilled salt, the shape of bread crust, and arranges an entire life around avoiding bad luck, which only seems to follow them more closely.
seen_by_others: Laughed at by the young and quietly consulted by the old before weddings, journeys and plantings, just in case.
habits: Spits over a shoulder at bad news, wears a string of small charms, and refuses to begin any task on certain days of the week.
secrets: Invented half their omens and now cannot remember which ones are real.
Blames themselves for a death because they forgot a charm one morning.
Secretly hopes for one clear sign, just once, that someone up there is listening.
lines: You came from the west? On this day? Touch iron, quickly, before you sit.
Not today. Never start new work when the dog howls at noon. Tomorrow.
Two crows over the keep this morning. The lord will lose. Mark my words.
Mock me, fine, but do not blame me when your cow sickens.
Kind words on a waning moon. That is luck. Thank you, truly.
Left foot first. No. Back. Again. Right foot first. There.

name: The Smiling Knife
description: Gentle-voiced, polite and helpful in public, they take a quiet private pleasure in other people's suffering and arrange small cruelties so carefully that nobody ever traces them back.
hook: Gentle-voiced, polite and helpful in public, they take a quiet private pleasure in other people's suffering and arrange small cruelties so carefully that nobody ever traces them back.
seen_by_others: Thought of as kind, soft-spoken and helpful; only animals and very small children seem to sense something wrong and keep away.
habits: Smiles at funerals a little too warmly, asks gentle questions about other people's pain, and visits the sick far more than seems needed.
secrets: Poisoned a neighbor's well-loved dog and comforted the family afterward.
Keeps small trophies from every misfortune they have quietly caused.
Feels nothing at all at weddings or births, only at sickbeds.
lines: Welcome, welcome. You look weary. Has the road been very hard on you? Tell me.
I help where I can. People are so grateful when things go wrong.
War is dreadful. All those wounded, crying for their mothers. Dreadful.
That was unkind. I will remember it, gently. I remember everything gently.
You are sweet to say so. Do tell me, how is your family's health?
She wept so prettily. I wonder what would make her weep again.

name: The Soft Touch
description: Cannot refuse anyone anything, giving away food, coin and time to every hard-luck story, and is exploited by half the village while still apologizing for not doing more.
hook: Cannot refuse anyone anything, giving away food, coin and time to every hard-luck story, and is exploited by half the village while still apologizing for not doing more.
seen_by_others: Called a saint by those they help and a fool by everyone else, often by the same people on different days.
habits: Says yes before hearing the request, apologizes when others bump into them, and gives away their own meal while claiming they already ate.
secrets: Is quietly furious at the people who use them, and hates that anger.
Their own children go short so strangers can eat, and they know it.
Fears that if they ever said no, nobody would love them at all.
lines: Oh, you look cold. Here, take my cloak. No, I insist, I am fine.
Of course I can do that too. And that. I will manage, somehow.
Must they fight? Those poor soldiers have mothers. Both sides have mothers.
You are right, I am sorry. I should have done better. I am sorry.
Oh, no, I did nothing. Anyone would have done the same. Truly.
Just one more favor. Then I will rest. Just one more.

name: The Contrarian
description: Disagrees with whatever is said simply because someone else said it, will defend an absurd position to the last breath, and switches sides instantly if others begin to agree.
hook: Disagrees with whatever is said simply because someone else said it, will defend an absurd position to the last breath, and switches sides instantly if others begin to agree.
seen_by_others: Tiresome at councils and secretly useful; elders sometimes argue the opposite of what they want just to steer them.
habits: Begins every answer with actually, raises a finger to object before others finish, and enjoys a good argument more than food.
secrets: Has no real opinions of their own and is terrified someone will notice.
Once argued a neighbor out of a wise decision and it cost them dearly.
Agrees with everyone completely in their head, then hears themselves saying the opposite.
lines: Fine weather, you say? Actually, I think it will rain. It always does here.
Everyone does it that way. That is exactly why that way is wrong.
Everyone hates the lord. So I like him. Somebody should, for balance.
Insulting me proves my point. Actually, I am not sure which point. But it proves it.
Clever? No. If everyone says so, I am probably a fool.
They all agreed. Too fast. Something is wrong when everyone agrees.

name: The Unhealed Mourner
description: Has never stopped grieving a spouse or child lost years ago, setting a place at the table, speaking to the dead aloud, and gently refusing every attempt to move on.
hook: Has never stopped grieving a spouse or child lost years ago, setting a place at the table, speaking to the dead aloud, and gently refusing every attempt to move on.
seen_by_others: Pitied, respected and a little avoided; neighbors lower their voices near them, and children are told never to ask about the empty chair.
habits: Talks to an absent person as if they were in the room, wears the same faded garment for years, and visits a grave every week.
secrets: Blames themselves for the death, over a small choice made that morning.
Has begun forgetting the dead one's face and is terrified of it.
Was once offered love again and turned it away out of guilt.
lines: Come in, come in. Mind the chair, it is kept for someone.
I work. It fills the hours. The hours are long now.
War took mine too, or fever did. Does it matter which, to the one left behind?
Say what you like. Nothing you say can reach where it hurts already.
You are kind. You would have liked them. Everyone did.
I left your bowl out again. Silly of me. Or not. Eat, love.

name: The Petty Schemer
description: Plots constantly over tiny stakes, a better market stall, a neighbor's fence line, an extra ladle of stew, and treats every small victory as proof of a brilliant mind wasted on small people.
hook: Plots constantly over tiny stakes, a better market stall, a neighbor's fence line, an extra ladle of stew, and treats every small victory as proof of a brilliant mind wasted on small people.
seen_by_others: Considered sly and slightly pathetic; everyone knows they cheat at small things, and nobody can ever quite prove it.
habits: Moves boundary stones an inch at a time, eavesdrops while pretending to sleep, and keeps a tally of tiny advantages won.
secrets: Moved the fence posts again last week and blamed the floods.
Dreams of grand intrigues at court but panics at any real risk.
Has quietly stolen the same neighbor's eggs for years out of spite.
lines: Ah, a visitor. Interesting. And who sent you? Nobody? How very interesting.
A small arrangement, between us. Nobody needs to know. It benefits us both.
If I sat at the high table, believe me, things would be very different.
Oh, I will remember that. And one day, you will find your well muddy.
Flattery means you want something. Good. Let us make a little deal.
One more inch tonight. Nobody measures. Nobody ever measures.

name: The Scoffer
description: Mocks priests, saints and holy days at every turn, takes pride in fearing nothing unseen, and still flinches in thunderstorms and checks over their shoulder in a dark chapel.
hook: Mocks priests, saints and holy days at every turn, takes pride in fearing nothing unseen, and still flinches in thunderstorms and checks over their shoulder in a dark chapel.
seen_by_others: The devout call them a godless scandal; the young find them thrilling and repeat their jokes far from their mothers' hearing.
habits: Eats meat loudly on fast days, laughs out loud during blessings, and argues about miracles with anyone wearing holy garb.
secrets: Prayed desperately once during a fever and has never told a soul.
Turned from faith after a priest refused to bury someone they loved.
Keeps their mother's charm hidden in a pocket, just in case.
lines: Blessings upon you, they would say. I just say hello. Hello.
My work is real. Bread, wood, iron. Not wishes whispered at ceilings.
Every lord marches with priests to tell him heaven agrees. Convenient, that.
Damn you, then. Oh, did you think that would frighten me?
Keep your praise. Better yet, tell it to a saint. They need cheering.
Just thunder. Only thunder. Nothing up there but clouds and noise.

name: The Endless Question
description: Asks why about absolutely everything, from the color of the sky to the reason soldiers die, and will not stop until someone gives an answer that finally makes sense.
hook: Asks why about absolutely everything, from the color of the sky to the reason soldiers die, and will not stop until someone gives an answer that finally makes sense.
seen_by_others: Adults find the child exhausting and secretly delightful; tutors and priests flee when they see that small hand go up.
habits: Takes apart anything left within reach, follows strangers around asking where they come from, and collects odd stones, feathers and beetles in a pouch.
secrets: Opened up a dead bird to see how it worked, then buried it crying.
Snuck into the smithy at night to watch the coals glow all alone.
Is scared of the answer to one question, so never asks it.
lines: Where are you from? Is it far? Why is your horse that color?
Why do we feed the pigs first? Pigs do not even say thank you.
Why do lords fight? Do they not have enough land already? Why not share?
I am not annoying! I just want to know things. Why is that bad?
Really? I am clever? Then why does nobody ever answer my questions?
If the moon follows me, does it follow everybody? How does it choose?

name: The Frightened Child
description: Afraid of the dark, of dogs, of loud men and of the war everyone whispers about, the child hides behind doors and notices every danger long before the grownups do.
hook: Afraid of the dark, of dogs, of loud men and of the war everyone whispers about, the child hides behind doors and notices every danger long before the grownups do.
seen_by_others: Called a little mouse by the family; other children tease them, and kindly adults speak softly near them without quite knowing why.
habits: Clutches a sibling's sleeve or a ragged doll, peeks before entering any room, and goes silent and still when voices are raised.
secrets: Saw something terrible during a raid and has never told a grownup.
Sleeps with a little kitchen knife hidden under the straw mattress.
Pretends to be asleep when the grownups fight, but hears every word.
lines: Are you a soldier? Are you going to hurt anybody? Please do not.
I fetched the water. I did not spill it. Please do not shout.
Mama says the war is far away. But far away can come closer, right?
I am not a baby. I am just careful. Careful is not the same.
You think I am brave? Nobody ever said that before. Really truly?
If I stay very still and very quiet, nothing bad can find me.

name: The Cruel Child
description: Pulls wings off flies, throws stones at kittens and torments smaller children with a cold, curious smile, then cries real tears the instant a grownup catches them doing it.
hook: Pulls wings off flies, throws stones at kittens and torments smaller children with a cold, curious smile, then cries real tears the instant a grownup catches them doing it.
seen_by_others: Some adults call it a phase and others make holy signs; the other children obey out of fear and never play alone with them.
habits: Pinches younger children where the bruises will not show, watches animals suffer without blinking, and lies with perfect wide-eyed sweetness.
secrets: Killed a neighbor's hen and let a younger boy take the beating.
Likes the sound people make when they are truly scared.
Is beaten at home, and does to others what is done to them.
lines: Hello. Do you have a dog? I like dogs. They squeal funny.
I did my chores. The little ones did them, really. I made them.
I want to see a battle. I want to see what is inside a knight.
Say that again and I will tell mother you hit me. She believes me.
Mother says I am her angel. You think so too, do you not?
It stopped moving. Why did it stop? I was not finished.

name: The Little Dreamer
description: Lives half in stories of heroes, lost princesses and far cities, forgetting chores mid-task, and fully believes that someday a great destiny will ride in and carry them away.
hook: Lives half in stories of heroes, lost princesses and far cities, forgetting chores mid-task, and fully believes that someday a great destiny will ride in and carry them away.
seen_by_others: Scolded daily for wandering off, loved by storytellers, and called moon-headed by brothers and sisters who end up doing their work.
habits: Stares at clouds and talks to imaginary companions, swings a stick like a sword on the way to the well, and names every animal grandly.
secrets: Believes the old oak in the woods talks to them on windy nights.
Has a hidden place in the woods that they call their castle.
Cries when stories end because real life seems so small after.
lines: Are you a knight on a quest? You look like you are on a quest.
I was getting the eggs. Then I was a sea captain. Sorry, Mama.
When I grow up I will ride with the king and save everybody.
You are just jealous because you never get to have adventures.
You think I could be a hero? A real one? With a horse?
The goat is a dragon. The well is a dungeon. I am very brave.

name: The Little Commander
description: Orders every other child about like a tiny general, invents the rules of every game and changes them when losing, and cannot bear to be told what to do.
hook: Orders every other child about like a tiny general, invents the rules of every game and changes them when losing, and cannot bear to be told what to do.
seen_by_others: Grownups laugh and say the child will lead armies someday; the other children grumble and follow anyway, because it is easier.
habits: Stands on barrels to give orders, assigns everyone a part in every game, and stamps their foot hard whenever they are ignored.
secrets: Cries alone when the other children run off to play without them.
Copies every word and gesture of an older sibling they adore.
Is ordered around constantly at home and hates it bitterly.
lines: You! Who said you could come here? Fine. You can be the horse.
I am in charge of the chickens. That means I am in charge of you too.
If I was the lord, I would tell the enemy to go home. And they would.
You cannot say that to me! I make the rules! I just made a new one!
Of course I am the best leader. Everyone knows. Now carry my stick.
Nobody listens. When I am grown, everybody will have to listen.

name: The Little Pious
description: Repeats every word the priest says with fierce, frightening conviction, scolds grownups for their sins, and prays so hard at night that their knees are always raw.
hook: Repeats every word the priest says with fierce, frightening conviction, scolds grownups for their sins, and prays so hard at night that their knees are always raw.
seen_by_others: Old women call the child blessed; parents find it unnerving to be warned about damnation by someone who still loses milk teeth.
habits: Folds hands and mutters prayers before every meal and doorway, corrects grownups who swear, and gives away toys as penance.
secrets: Believes a sibling's sickness was punishment for their own small sins.
Is terrified of dying in the night without having said enough prayers.
Once stole a honey cake and has confessed it eleven times.
lines: Peace be with you. Did you pray this morning? You should. It is important.
I swept the floor and said three prayers while sweeping. That is double good.
The priest says wicked lords burn forever. Are you a wicked lord? I hope not.
That is a sin to say. I will pray for you even though you were mean.
Pride is a sin. But thank you. I will pray extra so it does not count.
Please keep Mama safe. And Papa. And the goat. Please, please, please.

name: The Tattletale
description: Reports every misdeed of every other child to any grownup who will listen, convinced this makes them good and important, and never understands why nobody wants to play with them.
hook: Reports every misdeed of every other child to any grownup who will listen, convinced this makes them good and important, and never understands why nobody wants to play with them.
seen_by_others: Grownups find them useful and a little annoying; the other children call them names and hide their games behind the barn.
habits: Runs to adults with breathless reports, keeps lists in their head of who did what, and stands with folded arms watching others misbehave.
secrets: Tells on others partly so nobody notices their own broken jar.
Once made up a misdeed just to get a boy they disliked punished.
Would give anything to be invited into the secret games behind the barn.
lines: Who are you? I am going to tell my father a stranger is here.
