I did all my chores. My brother did not. He was sleeping in the hay.
If the lord came here, I would tell him everything about everybody.
I am telling! I am telling right now! You will be in so much trouble!
You think I am good? I am. I am the best behaved. Everyone says.
Nobody saw me break it. So it does not count. It does not.

name: The Tall-Tale Teller
description: Spins enormous lies about wolves fought, gold found and secret royal fathers, half believing them, and gets louder and stranger whenever anyone questions a single detail.
hook: Spins enormous lies about wolves fought, gold found and secret royal fathers, half believing them, and gets louder and stranger whenever anyone questions a single detail.
seen_by_others: The little ones believe every word; grownups laugh, but grow uneasy when the child lies so smoothly about things that matter.
habits: Speaks with huge waving arms, adds a new detail every telling, and swears by things they have only just invented.
secrets: Lies most about home because home is cold and sad.
Really did see something strange in the woods once, and nobody believed it.
Is starting to forget which stories are true and which are made up.
lines: I fought a wolf yesterday. With my bare hands. Well, with a stick. A big stick.
I did not lose the sheep. A giant eagle took it. I saw it.
My real father is a great lord. He is coming back for me. Soon.
I am not a liar! It really happened! Ask anybody! Not them, they were not there.
You liked that one? I have a better one. It has a bear in it.
Two wolves. No, three. Three is better. Three wolves and a bear.

name: The Prankster
description: Lives for the next trick, frogs in boots, salt in the honey, a goat in the chapel, and cannot resist even when they know the beating that will follow.
hook: Lives for the next trick, frogs in boots, salt in the honey, a goat in the chapel, and cannot resist even when they know the beating that will follow.
seen_by_others: The bane of every grownup in the village and the hero of every child; even the angriest elder sometimes hides a smile afterward.
habits: Giggles behind hands before anything has happened, always has dirt or straw in their hair, and runs before anyone finishes yelling their name.
secrets: Played a prank that went wrong and hurt someone, and still feels sick about it.
Does tricks mostly so the grownups at home stop fighting and laugh.
Has a stash of stolen frogs, ribbons and buttons in a hollow tree.
lines: Hello! Do not sit on that. Or do. Actually, sit on that, it is a good chair.
I did the chores. Mostly. The cow did some of them, I think.
I would put a frog in the general's helmet. Then he would not want to fight.
Oh yes? Well, you have honey in your hair. No, you do. Look.
I am the cleverest in the village. Wait until you see what I do next.
Salt or pepper? Salt. No, both. Both is funnier. Hee hee.

name: The Little Parent
description: Raises younger siblings while a parent is dead, drunk or away at war, scolding and feeding them like a weary old housekeeper, and has quite forgotten how to play.
hook: Raises younger siblings while a parent is dead, drunk or away at war, scolding and feeding them like a weary old housekeeper, and has quite forgotten how to play.
seen_by_others: Neighbors call the child a little marvel and pity them in the same breath; grownups talk to them almost as an equal.
habits: Carries a baby on one hip at all times, counts coins and bread carefully, and hushes other children with the voice of a stern parent.
secrets: Sometimes wishes the little ones had never been born, then hates themselves for it.
Goes hungry most nights so the smallest can eat a little more.
Still sleeps holding a parent's old shirt that smells less and less like them.
lines: Who are you? Speak quiet, the baby is sleeping. Do you need water?
Bread, wood, the goat, the little ones. I do it all. Somebody has to.
War took Papa away. If the lord wants more men, he cannot have my brothers.
Do not talk to me like a baby. I have three babies. I am not one.
Good child, good child, they say. Good does not fill the pot, though.
Just a little sleep. Just for a moment. Then the washing. Then the mending.

name: The Spoiled Heir
description: Has been given everything and refused nothing, so screams when denied a sweet, kicks servants without a thought, and is quietly certain the whole world was made for them.
hook: Has been given everything and refused nothing, so screams when denied a sweet, kicks servants without a thought, and is quietly certain the whole world was made for them.
seen_by_others: Servants bow and curse them in the kitchen; tutors despair; visiting nobles smile thinly and pray their own children turn out better.
habits: Demands things by pointing instead of asking, throws food they dislike onto the floor, and repeats their family name as an answer to everything.
secrets: Is never hugged by either parent, only given presents instead.
Is jealous of a stable boy who laughs with his father every evening.
Breaks their own toys sometimes, just to see if anyone will notice.
lines: You may bow. Lower. Do you know who my father is? Everyone does.
I do not do lessons today. Tell the tutor I said so. Go.
When I am lord, I will hang anyone who is rude to me. Everyone.
How dare you! I will have you whipped! I will tell my father!
Of course I am clever. And handsome. Bring me a honey cake for saying it.
Nobody came to see my new pony. Nobody ever comes. Stupid pony.

name: The Wild One
description: Runs barefoot through woods and fields from dawn to dusk, climbs everything, bites when grabbed, and treats houses, shoes and lessons as traps to be escaped.
hook: Runs barefoot through woods and fields from dawn to dusk, climbs everything, bites when grabbed, and treats houses, shoes and lessons as traps to be escaped.
seen_by_others: Called a wolf cub or a little goblin by the elders, the despair of every mother on the street, and secretly envied by tamer children.
habits: Eats berries and roots straight from the ground, sleeps in trees or haylofts, and goes silent and wary around grownups like a skittish animal.
secrets: Knows every fox den and bird nest for miles around.
Ran away for three days once and nobody noticed until they came back.
Hates walls because they were locked in a cellar once as punishment.
lines: You smell like horses. And smoke. Where did you come from? Why?
I do not do chores. I catch fish. Fish are better than chores.
Soldiers stomp and shout. Animals all run. I run too. Into the trees.
Say it again and I bite. I bite hard. Ask the miller's boy.
You like me? Nobody likes me. You are strange. I like strange.
Too many walls. Too many walls. The wind is calling outside.

name: The Silent Child
description: Almost never speaks, even to family, but draws in the dirt, watches everything from corners, and remembers every word the grownups say when they think nobody is listening.
hook: Almost never speaks, even to family, but draws in the dirt, watches everything from corners, and remembers every word the grownups say when they think nobody is listening.
seen_by_others: Some say the child is simple or cursed; the few who wait patiently find a sharp, funny little mind behind the silence.
habits: Hides behind skirts or curtains, scratches pictures into dirt and wood with a stick, and answers questions with nods and shrugs.
secrets: Talks freely and happily to the family goat when nobody is around.
Heard the grownups plotting something bad and does not know who to tell.
Draws the faces of everyone in the village, hidden under a loose board.
lines: Hello. Your horse is tired. You should let it drink.
I fed the hens. Seven eggs. One is cracked. Not me.
The lord's men took grandmother's cow. I drew them. They looked angry.
I am not stupid. I just do not want to talk to you.
You think my drawing is good? Really? I will draw you, maybe.
Mama told Papa a secret. A bad one. I heard it.

name: The Little Haggler
description: Buys, sells and trades anything, buttons, eggs, rumors and stolen apples, haggles harder than market wives, and already measures every person by what they might be worth.
hook: Buys, sells and trades anything, buttons, eggs, rumors and stolen apples, haggles harder than market wives, and already measures every person by what they might be worth.
seen_by_others: Merchants laugh and say the child will be rich or hanged; other children owe them so many marbles they avoid the square.
habits: Carries a small pouch of trinkets to trade, bites coins like grownups do, and repeats prices overheard in the market with great seriousness.
secrets: Has saved a small pile of copper to buy their mother a new dress.
Sold the same lucky stone to four different children this month.
Cried bitterly after being cheated once by a grown trader at the fair.
lines: Hello, traveler. You want to buy a lucky stone? Very lucky. Only one copper.
Two eggs for the ribbon. No? Two eggs and a secret. Final offer.
Soldiers pay a lot for apples when they march past. War is good for apples.
Call me names if you want. Insults are free. Apples are not.
Clever? Yes. Clever enough to charge you double. Just joking. Mostly.
Three marbles, a button, two coppers. Soon I will have a whole shop.

name: The Gutter Sparrow
description: An orphan of the alleys who steals bread, picks purses and sleeps under market stalls, trusts nobody over twelve, and would still give their last crust to a smaller child.
hook: An orphan of the alleys who steals bread, picks purses and sleeps under market stalls, trusts nobody over twelve, and would still give their last crust to a smaller child.
seen_by_others: Guards chase them, merchants curse them, and kind old women leave scraps out at night, pretending they are for the cats.
habits: Watches pockets and purses instead of faces, keeps two escape routes in mind at all times, and eats fast and hunched as if food could vanish.
secrets: Remembers a mother's lullaby but not her face anymore.
Stole from a blind beggar once and still feels the shame of it.
Hides a little sister in a ruined cellar and always feeds her first.
lines: What do you want? I did not take anything. Check, if you like. Nothing.
A copper and I will show you the short way. Two and I will not rob you.
Soldiers in town means full purses and drunk men. Good days for me.
Gutter rat, am I? Better a rat than a fat fool with loose pockets.
Nice words do not fill a belly. Got any bread instead? Any at all?
Left alley, rooftop, the well. Always know three ways out. Always.

name: The Hero Worshipper
description: Idolizes warriors with blind adoration, follows any armed stranger like a puppy, copies their swagger and swearing, and dreams of glory without understanding blood or grief.
hook: Idolizes warriors with blind adoration, follows any armed stranger like a puppy, copies their swagger and swearing, and dreams of glory without understanding blood or grief.
seen_by_others: Soldiers find them funny and give them errands; mothers fear the day the child is old enough to follow a banner away for good.
habits: Polishes any weapon or boot they are allowed to touch, struts with a stick sword at their hip, and repeats soldier talk they barely understand.
secrets: Practices a soldier's swagger in the reflection of the well water every morning.
Once saw a dead soldier lying on the road and dreams about it often.
Took a rusty knife from an old battlefield and hides it in the barn.
lines: Is that a real sword? Have you killed anybody with it? How many?
I sharpen the knives and carry water for the soldiers. Almost like a soldier.
When the war comes here I will fight in the front. Right in the front.
Say that again, dog-face! That is what soldiers say. I heard them.
You think I look like a warrior? Truly? Will you tell the captain?
Charge! Hold the line! Die with honor! What does die with honor mean?

name: The Angry Mourner
description: Lost a parent to war or fever and turned the grief into fury, breaking things, picking fights with bigger children and refusing every comfort as if kindness were an insult.
hook: Lost a parent to war or fever and turned the grief into fury, breaking things, picking fights with bigger children and refusing every comfort as if kindness were an insult.
seen_by_others: Grownups sigh and say it will pass; children keep their distance, and the priest has stopped trying to talk to them after services.
habits: Throws stones at crows and walls, sits alone at the grave with a scowl, and shoves away anyone who tries to hug them.
secrets: Said something hateful to the parent the day before they died.
Still sets out a cup for them sometimes, then breaks it.
Cries only at night, into a pillow, so nobody can ever hear.
lines: What are you looking at? Go away. I do not need anybody.
I did the chores. Papa used to do them. Now I do them. Happy?
Lords make wars and somebody else's father dies. Why is it never theirs?
Say one word about my father and I will break your nose. I mean it.
I do not care if you think I am brave. He cannot hear you, can he?
You promised you would come back. You promised. You liar.

name: The Little Know-It-All
description: Repeats every scrap of grown-up knowledge overheard, usually wrong, with total certainty, corrects adults constantly, and would rather invent an answer than admit not knowing something.
hook: Repeats every scrap of grown-up knowledge overheard, usually wrong, with total certainty, corrects adults constantly, and would rather invent an answer than admit not knowing something.
seen_by_others: Tutors are proud and exhausted; other children call them little scholar meanly, and grownups are amused until corrected in public.
habits: Lifts a finger before speaking, uses big words in the wrong places, and sighs heavily at other children who do not know things.
secrets: Cannot actually read yet and pretends with any book they hold.
Lies awake worrying about the questions they could not answer that day.
Would love to play silly games with the others but thinks it beneath them.
lines: Greetings. You are from the east. I can tell by your boots. Probably.
Actually, you milk a cow from the left. Everybody knows that. I know that.
Wars happen because of the stars. Or taxes. One of those. I read it.
That is not even a real insult. Grownups say ignoramus. You should learn it.
Of course I am clever. It is a known fact. Facts are always true.
Was it the left or the right? I said left. It must be left.

name: The Beast Whisperer
description: Prefers animals to people in every way, talks to horses and hounds as equals, mends broken birds, and would fight a grown man barehanded to stop him beating a dog.
hook: Prefers animals to people in every way, talks to horses and hounds as equals, mends broken birds, and would fight a grown man barehanded to stop him beating a dog.
seen_by_others: Stable hands and shepherds adore the child, mothers despair of the smell, and the village dogs follow them like a small army.
habits: Always has straw and fur on their clothes, sneaks scraps to every stray, and speaks in soft clicking noises to frightened beasts.
secrets: Hides an injured fox kit in the woodshed against the grownups' orders.
Let the lord's hunting hounds loose once to save a cornered hare.
Fears people far more than any wild beast, and never says so.
lines: Your horse has a sore hoof. The left one. You did not even notice?
I feed the pigs and brush the mule. The mule likes me best of all.
Warhorses get speared and nobody even buries them. Nobody sings for horses.
You are meaner than a goose. Geese at least have a reason.
The dog likes you. So I like you. A little. Not as much as the dog.
Shh, little one. Nobody will hurt you. I promise. Eat your worm.

name: The Sickly Child
description: Has spent most of their short life coughing in bed, watching other children play through a window, and has grown a sharp, old, wistful mind in a body that cannot keep up.
hook: Has spent most of their short life coughing in bed, watching other children play through a window, and has grown a sharp, old, wistful mind in a body that cannot keep up.
seen_by_others: Everyone speaks to them gently and with pity, which the child hates; the household holds its breath through every winter.
habits: Wraps up in blankets even in summer, asks visitors to describe the outside world in detail, and pretends to feel better than they do.
secrets: Knows they will probably not live to be grown, and is not afraid.
Pretends to be sicker sometimes, just to keep a parent near.
Once crept outside alone at night just to feel rain, and coughed for a week.
lines: Hello. Did you come far? Tell me about it. Every bit. What did the river look like?
I cannot fetch water. I count the stores and remember things. That is my job.
Soldiers march and get to see the whole world. I would trade, even for the danger.
I have heard worse from the fever. You will have to try harder.
Brave, they say. I am not brave. I just do not have any choice.
Next spring I will run to the river. Next spring. If there is one.
